name: Harkonen
label: Hydra Head
lede: A five-piece from Tacoma that shed members until a trio was left, then made two Hydra Head records and a stack of splits before quitting at Bumbershoot.

eras.title: Five guys, then fewer
eras.text: Harkonen started in Tacoma as a five-piece noisy hardcore band and went through singers and guitarists fast. By the end of the decade the group was down to a trio.

years.h: Debut 7" on Unjust, then two founders are gone
years.p: Harkonen's self-titled 7" came out on Unjust in 1997. Vocalist Mike Jones and guitarist Chris Vancourt left soon after, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Label bio text describes the band at this point as a five-piece hardcore band in the vein of Deadguy and Kiss It Goodbye. The name comes from the Harkonnen family in Frank Herbert's Dune.

years.h: Hung to Dry 7" and a new vocalist, Aaron Connell
years.p: Harkonen followed up with the Hung to Dry 7" on Excursion. Aaron "Edge" Connell joined on vocals; he later founded [[Himsa|198bed0f-a246-4116-9c7a-0140cbd372b7]].
years.xp: Wikipedia says Connell came over from Grip and left around 1999 along with guitarist Neihl Brady. Last.fm's bio says he left to focus on other projects, including Himsa. Wikipedia's Himsa page lists him in that band from 1998 to 1999.

years.p: The first full-length came out on Wreck-Age, and the group settled as a trio: Ben Verellen, Casey Hardy and Matt Howard.
years.xp: Sources disagree on who played what and when guitarist Bill Quinby left. Wikipedia has him gone around 1999 and the trio of Verellen, Hardy and Howard holding through 2005.

eras.title: Hydra Head takes them in
eras.text: As a trio Harkonen moved from Deadguy-style hardcore toward noise rock, and landed on Aaron Turner's label. Two records for Hydra Head are what most people know them for.

years.p: The CD followed the self-titled album and came out on the small label Ataque Sonoro, a year before the move to Hydra Head.

years.h: Grizz: first release on Hydra Head Records
years.p: Five songs, including "Kildow's Song" and "Hey You Millionaires, Get Out of That Garbage." It came as a CD EP and a 7" on [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]]'s label.
years.xp: Harkonen went on to tour nationally with Hydra Head bands including Isis, according to Last.fm's bio.

years.h: Shake Harder Boy: 11 songs in about 27 minutes
years.p: Recorded with [[Matt Bayles|e294077f-71eb-401f-a36a-f2dbcbd75863]] at Studio Litho and Avast! Recording Co. The set includes "Smile Pretty," "Baristas Get Stalked" and the 5:29 closer "Settle Here."
years.xp: Wikipedia credits the production to Bayles and the band. One reviewer at vaguely-offensive gave it five out of five and put it next to [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]] and Pelican for pummeling heft that still left room for experiments.

years.h: Ben Verellen starts Roy with his brother Dave, of [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]]
years.p: Roy was a Tacoma folk and country-leaning rock band with Dave Verellen and Brian Cook, both ex-Botch, and Ben Verellen.
years.xp: Roy released its EPs starting in 2002, then Big City Sin and Small Town Redemption in 2004 on Fueled by Ramen, made with Matt Bayles. Dave Verellen said in 2009 that nobody bought the records, and he was fine with that.

years.p: The last solo release, out on Initial Records. One reviewer called it looser than Shake Harder Boy.

eras.title: Splits, then Bumbershoot
eras.text: The last two years were split releases and the end of the band. Harkonen's final show was at a Seattle festival.

years.p: Released on Happy Couples Never Last, per Wikipedia's discography.

yt: Payday Loans, split with These Arms Are Snakes
years.h: Like a Virgin split with These Arms Are Snakes
years.p: Harkonen's last release, a split EP with the Seattle band These Arms Are Snakes. Ben Verellen also played additional bass on their debut and briefly drummed for them on tour in 2005.
years.xp: Discogs and YouTube list the split as 2004 or 2005, so the date is uncertain. Wikipedia's Ben Verellen article says he was These Arms Are Snakes' touring drummer in 2005.

years.h: Last show at Bumbershoot in Seattle
years.p: Harkonen ended in 2005 after nearly eight years, with a final performance at Seattle's Bumbershoot festival.
years.xp: The Brutal Panda label bio says Harkonen "stormed the northwest music scene for nearly eight years." Last.fm says the band began losing momentum around the final EP.

eras.title: Helms Alee and a Botch reunion cover
eras.text: Nothing from Harkonen itself after 2005, but Ben Verellen kept going in other bands and around old friends.

years.p: Verellen's next long-running band, Helms Alee, has put out seven albums since 2008, per Wikipedia. He also builds guitar amps under Verellen Amplifiers.

years.h: Verellen joins [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] and Botch's Dimitri Minakakis for a Botch cover
years.p: For Two Minutes to Late Night's Hardcore Summer series, they played Botch's "To Our Friends in the Great White North." Verellen had also sung backing vocals at Botch's last show, per Louder.
